tasks.title: Free-space path loss
tasks.statement: Distance **{d} km**, frequency **{f} MHz**. Find the FSPL (dB).
tasks.solution: FSPL = 20·lg(d_km) + 20·lg(f_MHz) + 32.44. Doubling the distance or the frequency adds 6 dB.

tasks.title: Link margin
tasks.statement: Transmitter **{p} dBm**, antennas of **{g} dBi** at both ends, FSPL **{l} dB**, receiver sensitivity **−{s} dBm**. Find the margin (dB).
tasks.solution: Margin = P_tx + G_tx + G_rx − FSPL − S_rx (the sensitivity is negative, so you add its absolute value). The minimum is 10–15 dB for fading; 20 dB is comfortable.

tasks.title: Fresnel zone
tasks.statement: A **{d} km** link at **{f} GHz**. Find the radius of the first Fresnel zone at mid-path (m).
tasks.solution: r₁ = 17.32·√(d_km/(4·f_GHz)) at mid-path. 60 % of this radius must be clear of obstacles.

tasks.title: Range from margin
tasks.statement: At a distance of **{d0} km** the calculated link margin is **{m0} dB** (free space). At what distance will the margin fall to **{m} dB** (km)?
tasks.solution: FSPL grows as 20·lg(d), so d = d₀·10^((M₀ − M)/20): every 6 dB of margin doubles the range. The module's example: 29.8 dB at 1 km → 12 dB at 1·10^(17.8/20) ≈ 7.8 km.

tasks.title: Radio horizon
tasks.statement: The transmitter antenna at a height of **{h1} m**, the aircraft at **{h2} m**. Find the radio horizon range with k = 4/3 (km).
tasks.solution: d = √(2kRh₁) + √(2kRh₂), R = 6371 km, k = 4/3 → d ≈ 4.12·(√h₁ + √h₂) km with h in meters. The module's example: 2 m and 120 m → 51 km. Beyond the horizon the link drops abruptly, whatever the FSPL margin.

tasks.title: Two-ray model breakpoint
tasks.statement: Frequency **{f} MHz**, ground antenna at **{h1} m**, aircraft at **{h2} m**. Find the breakpoint distance d_c = 4·h₁·h₂/λ (km).
tasks.solution: λ = c/f = 299.79/f(MHz) m; d_c = 4·h₁·h₂/λ. Beyond the breakpoint the power falls at 40 dB per decade (12 dB per doubling) instead of 20. The module's example: 2440 MHz, 1.5 and 10 m → λ = 0.123 m, d_c = 0.49 km.
